title: Fabric counts explained
subtitle: How the count number on needlework fabric translates to stitch size and finished dimensions.
excerpt: The count number on a fabric label tells you how many stitches fit in one inch. A higher count means more stitches per inch and a smaller finished size. Understanding this lets you adapt any chart to any cloth.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Fabric selection and stitch size guidance.
Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Internet Archive. Count and ground cloth principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: The number of cross-stitches that fit in one inch of fabric. On Aida, this is the fabric count number. On evenweave stitched over two threads, this is half the fabric count.

content.text: The count number on a fabric label tells you how many
stitches per inch

the cloth will give. On Aida, 14-count means 14 stitches per inch. On evenweave, 28-count means 14 stitches per inch when you stitch over two threads. The same chart will produce different finished sizes on different counts.
How to calculate finished size
Find the chart's stitch count: the number of stitches across the width and down the height. Most charts print this.
Divide each number by the effective stitch count of your chosen cloth.
The result is the design size in inches. Multiply by 2.54 to get centimetres.
Add at least 5 cm on each side for the hoop or framing border.
Quick reference: effective stitch counts
11-count Aida: 11 stitches per inch. Stitch is approximately 2.3 mm square.
14-count Aida: 14 stitches per inch. Stitch is approximately 1.8 mm square.
16-count Aida: 16 stitches per inch. Stitch is approximately 1.6 mm square.
18-count Aida: 18 stitches per inch. Stitch is approximately 1.4 mm square.
25-count evenweave over two threads: 12.5 stitches per inch.
28-count evenweave over two threads: 14 stitches per inch. Matches 14-count Aida in stitch size.
32-count linen over two threads: 16 stitches per inch.
Common mistakes

items.symptom: The finished piece is much smaller than the chart specified
items.cause: The chart's specified count was different from the cloth used, or the evenweave count was not halved for the over-two calculation.
items.fix: Check the chart's stated count. A chart for 14-count Aida stitched on 18-count Aida produces a piece 78% of the intended size.

items.symptom: There isn't enough fabric to finish the design
items.cause: Not enough border margin was added when cutting.
items.fix: Add at least 5 cm margin on all sides when cutting. For a framed piece, 8 cm is safer.

content.text: What this underpins
Count arithmetic underpins every pattern in the library. Understanding
fabric count
lets you substitute fabric freely and calculate how much cloth to buy without guesswork.
